reason: The cited evidence (E1-E4) supports low friction and wear of the specific coating at room temperature in ambient air via a tribocatalytic mechanism, but provides no data or mechanistic evidence for performance above room temperature, in inert environments, or with an adhesion interlayer. The key premises regarding high-temperature efficacy, environmental versatility, and interlayer function are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Spray-coated (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflakes provide low COF (~0.076) and wear rate (~10^-9 mm3/Nm) at room temperature under high contact pressure in ambient air.
The low friction and wear are due to shear-induced tribocatalytic activity forming a self-lubricating tribolayer.
This tribocatalytic self-lubrication mechanism will remain effective and continuously regenerative from room temperature up to 800 °C.
An adhesion-promoting interlayer will ensure coating integrity and tribolayer stability across the full temperature range.
The coating will maintain low COF and wear under variable loads (0.5–1.0 GPa) and in both ambient and inert environments.
